title: Ops + Seller Microworkshop Blueprint (draft)
content:
Purpose: provide a lightweight, repeatable 30–60 minute hands-on workshop sellers can run with platform/integration engineers to accelerate pilot validation and surface operational risk quickly.

Intended audience: sales engineers, platform sellers, customer engineering, early-stage enterprise buyers (platform + infra personas).

Workshop outcomes (30–60m):
- Quick signal whether the buyer can integrate Redwood in a pilot window (networking, auth, latency baseline).
- Measurable latency & cost ballpark for representative workload (3 short scenarios).
- Runbook of immediate blockers and mitigations — enabling a clear next-step: pilot-runbook or executive summary.

Format options (pick one):
- 30m Rapid Triage: 10m setup + 10m live tests + 10m triage & next steps.
- 60m Deep Smoke Test: 15m setup + 25m multi-scenario tests + 20m analysis & mitigation design.

Facilitator script (concise):
- Intro (2 min): Purpose + outcome commitments. "By the end of this session we'll know if a pilot can start within X days and what the biggest integration risks are."
- Ask for quick architecture sketch (3 min): who controls network/firewalls, where secrets live, expected call volumes.
- Run the tests (live): coach through the checks, call out what to observe.
- Close: confirm owner for pilot tasks and set clear follow-up (Jira ticket + pilot timeline).

Slide-by-slide notes (speaker-friendly):
1) Title + target outcome (30s)
2) Agenda & timing (30s)
3) Quick buyer checklist (2 min): network, auth, model choice, throughput expectations
4) Live test plan (1 min): three short scenarios (see below)
5) Demo preflight checklist (1 min): API key, region, test dataset ready, sample prompt set
6) Run scenario 1: low-latency single-turn queries (10m) - measure p50/p95, token counts, error surface
7) Run scenario 2: chat-like multi-turn (15m) - observe KV cache behavior, token growth, model variant fallback
8) Run scenario 3: embeddings/search workload (10m) - throughput, vector size, batching effects
9) Triage board (5m): blockers, mitigations, owner assignment
10) Next steps & pilot gating criteria (2 min)

Three scenario templates (what to run):
- Scenario A: User-facing autocomplete (p50 < 200ms target). Run 50 single requests, measure latency distribution, note cold-starts.
- Scenario B: Session-based assistant (context window ~2k tokens). Run 20 multi-turn dialogues, measure memory growth, observe quality regressions after truncation.
- Scenario C: Bulk embedding batch (10k rows simulation). Run mini-batch of 256 vectors, track throughput and estimated per-1000-unit cost.

Quick metrics to capture (minimum):
- p50/p95 latency, failure rate, tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens or embeddings, observed throughput under test batch size.

Triage checklist (common blockers & mitigation snippets):
- Network (blocked outbound to Redwood region): mitigation: request firewall rule for outbound 443 to region/reserved IP; offer test via temporary tunnelling option.
- Auth (internal KMS/HSM constraints): mitigation: demo with short-lived key, map how KMS integration timeline looks (private deployments).
- Data residency / compliance: mitigation: propose Private mode or Dedicated with contract Q&A.
- Latency too high in region: mitigation: switch to regional endpoint or smaller model + quantized variant; document tradeoffs.
- Tokenization surprises (unexpected tokens per prompt): mitigation: run tokenizer inspection, craft prompt templates to reduce tokens.

Decision heuristics (how we recommend sellers decide to push a pilot):
- Green: pilot within 2 weeks if p95 < target SLA, obvious owners, and no compliance blocker.
- Yellow: pilot with constraints if a mitigatable single blocker exists (network/auth) and customer committed resources.
- Red: schedule pre-pilot engineering engagement if multiple blockers or architecture mismatch.

Ownership & follow-up artifacts to create during/after workshop:
- Create a lightweight Jira ticket (template included in linked_artifacts) capturing: blocker, owner, ETA, mitigation.
- Produce a 1-page pilot summary: baseline metrics, gap list, recommended model & config, estimated cost. Use the internal template on Confluence.

Quick scripts & snippets (copy-paste for demo):
- Simple cURL check (auth + ping): curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Minimal generation request (single-shot): POST /v1/generate with prompt slice and small max_tokens to measure latency.
- Embedding batch sample script (python) with batch size param to show throughput scaling.

Risk signals (what to watch for live):
- Repeated 500s or timeouts during low load -> indicates infra misrouting or proxy issues.
- High token count variance -> prompt engineering needed.
- Persistent p95 spikes only in customer region -> network path or peering issue.

Sales enablement checklist (before running the workshop):
- Confirm buyer participants: SE + platform lead + network owner if possible.
- Prep sample prompts and small dataset (anonymized).
- Reserve Redwood test model quotas and a cluster region.
- Pre-create a Confluence note and Jira epic placeholder.

Templates included (to copy into decks or emails):
- Workshop invite blurb (short): "30m shop: quick smoke test to validate pilot feasibility — we’ll run 3 quick tests and leave with a clear next step. Please bring your platform engineer if possible."
- Post-workshop summary headings: baseline metrics, blockers, recommended pilot config, owners & deadlines.

How sellers should position this to buyers (script):
- "We run a focused technical smoke test to reduce three biggest unknowns for a pilot: latency, auth/network, and integration effort. It’s short, repeatable, and designed to get you to a safe pilot decision in 1–2 weeks."

Open questions (for iteration):
- How much automation do we want in the post-session ticket creation? (Jira API integration suggested)
- Should we ship a small test harness in the SDK specifically for these microworkshops?
- Any legal-approved language for transient keys / tunnelling we must standardize?

Next steps for GTM team:
- Pilot this blueprint with 3 seller teams in March; capture timings and blocker frequency.
- Iterate the slide templates based on feedback and move to a finalized 1-pager + 6-slide living deck.

Notes to self:
- Keep scripts short; sellers skip heavy infra steps. Focus on decision grade signals.
- Add a one-slide quick-cost-estimator for each scenario (approx per-1k tokens or per-1000 embeddings).

References and internal links: see linked_artifacts above for ticket template, Confluence playbook, and the ops-playbooks PR that contains sample scripts.

Last edited notes: Maya added the 3 scenario templates on 2025-02-22; Liam added the triage checklist 2025-02-26.
